newsitem.title: USA: Goldman says pound overvalued by near 15 percent.
newsitem.headline: Goldman says pound overvalued by near 15 percent.

text.p: The pound is significantly overvalued and market expectations for a rise to 3.0 marks are "daft", according to Goldman Sachs and Co.
"The pound is overvalued by close to 15 percent at current levels," the firm said in its London-based publication The Weekly Analyst, dated Tuesday June 24.
AT 1140 EDT/1540 GMT on Tuesday, the pound was quoted at 2.8728/38 marks, below its earlier 59-month high of 2.8818.
Goldman said sterling's rise above 2.87 marks on Monday coincided with increased market talk of an advance to 3.00 marks.

While the investment bank said a further rise is indeed possible, it added buying sterling/mark at 2.87 with a 3.00 target in mind is "not quite, but nearly as daft as" buying dollar/yen at 127.00 for a possible target of 130.00.
The firm recommended staying square sterling for now, with a view to sell rather than buy.
